name: Structural cue: singleton pair_id (no reversed twin in the file) => NEGATIVE_OTHER
links: Data and file format: https://inigolopezgazpio.net/SemEval-2027-Task-2-DiCo-NLI/final_data/ (GitHub ilopezgazpio/SemEval-2027-Task-2-DiCo-NLI) ; rules (invalid / deceptive submissions, mandatory reporting): https://inigolopezgazpio.net/SemEval-2027-Task-2-DiCo-NLI/ ; analogous dataset-artifact literature: Gururangan et al. 2018 'Annotation Artifacts in NLI Data' (arXiv:1803.02324), Poliak et al. 2018 'Hypothesis Only Baselines in NLI' (arXiv:1805.01042). In-repo anchor: src/labels.py parse_instance_id / reverse_instance_id.
license_access: Not a model; zero cost, rule-based. Legitimacy depends on the final task rules and on the organizers' view.
track_coverage: All four tracks in train/dev. Verified on the released files: in every track, reversible items always come as a twin pair (2 rows per pair_id per language view) while every NEGATIVE_OTHER item is a single row in 'original' orientation (T1-T3 train: 1,282 twin pairs + 478 singletons; T4 train: 7,692 twin views + 2,868 singletons = 478 x 6 language combos). A second, even simpler cue also holds: reversible items use pair_id numbers 1-1,946 (the PhrasIS reversible source set size) and NEG items use 1,947-3,320 (train min 1,947 / dev min 1,949).
basque_quality: Not applicable: language-independent, works identically in EN, ES, EU and mixed tracks.
cross_lingual_robustness: Identical behavior across languages because it ignores text; in T4 the twin swaps languages (en-es original <-> es-en flipped) and reverse_instance_id() already handles that.
architecture: Rule: for each test row, compute its twin id with reverse_instance_id() (swap languages, original<->flipped) or, id-free, search for a row whose (text1, text2) equals this row's (text2, text1). If no twin exists, predict NEGATIVE_OTHER; otherwise restrict the classifier to {EQ, FE, BE} and decode the pair jointly. Variants: (a) hard override; (b) soft feature (twin_present flag fed to the model or used as a prior); (c) id-range rule pair_number > 1946 => NEG (most brittle).
sample_efficiency: Perfect on train/dev: precision = recall = 1.0 for NEG on all released splits and tracks (no reversible item lacks its twin; no NEG item has one). It needs no training data.
reported_results: Computed on the released data: the rule classifies NEGATIVE_OTHER with 100% precision and recall on T1-T4 train (478 / 478, 2,868 / 2,868) and dev (106 / 106, 636 / 636), which makes NEG F1 = 1.0 and removes all reversible-vs-NEG confusion, leaving only the 3-way EQ/FE/BE decision on twin pairs. With a base model whose NEG F1 is ~0.6-0.8 and which sends some reversible pairs to NEG, this would add several points of Weighted F1 (NEG is ~16% of rows) and some HardCons [uncertain]. No external reports.
pilot_dico_results: Not applicable; the pilot used only positive (reversible) combined tracks, without NEG items.
consistency_guarantee: none by itself (it only fixes NEG); combined with 3-way joint decoding on twins it yields SoftCons = 1.0 on all reversible pairs, since no reversible pair can be sent to NEG
negative_other_handling: NEG is decided purely by twin absence; with the override the system can never emit NEG on a row that has a twin, so it cannot emit NEG on any reversible pair.
metric_tradeoff: If the test file keeps the train/dev structure: Weighted F1 up (NEG class perfect, no reversible rows lost to NEG), HardCons up (no reversible pairs sacrificed to NEG), SoftCons up to its maximum with joint decoding. If the test file differs (e.g. NEG items also given in both orders, ids anonymised and shuffled, or reversible items included without their twins), the hard rule can catastrophically fail: every twin-less reversible item becomes NEG (hurting all three scores) and NEG items with twins are never predicted NEG.
integration: A post-processing step in the decoding script: build the set of instance_ids (and a (text2, text1) lookup for the id-free version), mark singletons, override to NEG, and pass only twin pairs to joint decoding. Implement behind a flag (--structural-cue off|feature|override) so a cue-free submission is always available and ablations can be reported.
ensemble_compatibility: Compatible as a post-hoc override on top of any ensemble; as a feature it would bias calibration, so keep it outside the probability pooling.
rules_disclosure: Current public rules do not prohibit using instance_id/pair_id structure, but organizers 'may withhold scores for ... deceptive ... or rule-violating submissions', and all techniques must be described in the system paper. Exploiting a construction artifact that makes one class trivially predictable is likely to be seen as against the spirit of a task that explicitly aims to test whether systems 'separate directional entailment from weaker or unrelated semantic relations'. Recommended: raise it with the organizers (GitHub issue / email inigo.lopez@ehu.eus) before the evaluation phase, submit the cue-free system as primary unless explicitly permitted, and report cue-based results only as a disclosed ablation.
contamination: Not a data-contamination issue, but a label leakage through metadata (the file structure reveals the NEG label). The id-range variant additionally reveals that DiCo pair numbers follow PhrasIS ordering, i.e. that reversible pairs are the first 1,946 PhrasIS items, which is also a hint that test gold labels are recoverable from public PhrasIS (see auxiliary-data item).
structural_cue_dependence: Total by definition. Robustness if test metadata differs: the id-based variants break if ids are anonymised; the text-swap variant survives anonymisation but still breaks if organizers add reversed NEG items or drop twins. Organizers are likely to fix this artifact once noticed (e.g. by adding NEG in both orders, since SoftCons ignores NEG anyway) [uncertain].
priority: P0 for the action 'ask the organizers and keep a cue-free primary system'; P2 for relying on it in a ranked submission (only if explicitly permitted). Use it freely as a diagnostic upper bound on dev (it tells how many points are lost to NEG confusion).
expected_gain: Conditional: if permitted and the test keeps the train/dev structure, roughly +3 to +8 W-F1 and +1 to +5 HardCons over a strong model without it, depending on how well the model already separates NEG [uncertain]. Risk-adjusted value for the official ranking is low to negative: potential disqualification or reputational cost, and total failure if the test format changes. Its most valuable legitimate uses are as a dev-time oracle for estimating the NEG-confusion ceiling and as motivation for a strong learned NEG gate.
